# 0.2.4 - November 2026 LTS maintenance

This release hardens serial transactions, reduces ESP8266 static RAM use,
and limits diagnostic traffic without adding continuous receiver polling.

## Highlights

- Match acknowledgements to the command, report value and Extended selector.
  Unrelated reports cannot complete a pending write; all mapped responses for
  shared DSP/input commands are accepted across the eight explicit profiles.
- Use consistent retry and power-on timing policies. Relative, toggle and
  unknown writes are not retried; typed volume steps use bounded absolute
  targets and honor the configured half-dB step.
- Validate frame lengths, checksums and numeric reports, preserve Extended
  text/padding, and handle maximum-size frames and fragmented input.
- Refresh HA option metadata after late model detection, inherit configured
  volume limits, and keep parse-error states within HA's state length limit.
- Store all 666 command aliases in a deduplicated flash string pool. The
  ESP8266 full example uses 44,144 bytes of static RAM instead of 58,756
  (24.9% less); flash rises from 475,360 to 483,540 bytes (1.7%). These are
  linker measurements on the pinned build baseline, not runtime heap figures.
- Publish noisy diagnostics at a 60-second default interval, with counters
  only when changed. Noisy diagnostics are disabled by default in HA.
- Keep Dependabot security updates enabled without routine version-update PRs.

## Upgrade Notes

- Raw actions, aliases and raw media-player shortcuts now require
  `allow_raw_commands: true`. Native API raw access also requires API encryption.
  The full/x500 examples opt in; Basic leaves raw access disabled.
- Volume numbers inherit the parent's limits. Explicit number limits must fit
  within them; typed volume steps wait until the current volume is known.
- Existing HA entity-registry enable/disable choices are preserved. Full
  rejected frames are in debug logs, not the parse-error entity state.
- Read [Maintenance and Migration](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/v0.2.4/docs/maintenance.md)
  for event-driven availability, recorder load and memory measurement details.

## Validation and Limits

The build baseline remains ESPHome 2026.10.1, with HA companion runtime tests
on Home Assistant 2026.10.4. CI covers Python 3.12-3.14, production C++ tests
and fuzzing with sanitizers, all eight explicit profiles, minimum ESPHome
configuration validation, and ESP32/ESP8266 firmware builds with size budgets.

Known host-dependency vulnerabilities remain: stable ESPHome pins Pillow
12.3.0 and filelock 4.0.10; the HA test baseline also pins Pillow 12.3.0.
Compatible dependency fixes are constrained, but these exact upstream pins
are not forcibly overridden. These Python packages are not embedded in the
ESP firmware. See the [Security Policy](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/v0.2.4/SECURITY.md)
for exposure reductions and the remaining limitations. This release is not
declared vulnerability-free.

No firmware or HA integration is installed automatically. No new hardware
validation is claimed; model-specific command coverage still needs real-device
testing. Source/sound-mode selection in the receiver media player still needs
the optional HA companion; the native ESPHome entity does not advertise those
unsupported feature flags.
